newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister says allies discuss elections.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister says allies discuss elections.

text.p: A Turkish cabinet minister said on Tuesday that the two wings of the Islamist-led coalition were discussing elections amid a government crisis over Moslem activism.
"Elections are on the agenda. That is what we are debating," State Minister Salim Ensarioglu told reporters before a planned cabinet meeting.
"The date is not certain," he said when asked about the timing of any early polls. The next elections must be held by the year 2000.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition with pro-Western consrvatives has been slowly unravelling since the secularist generals demanded a crackdown on Islamist activism in February.
Three ministers from Ensarioglu's conservative True Path Party wing of the government have resigned in the last month.
Erbakan and coalition partner Tansu Ciller, the foreign minister, went into a one-to-one meeting at the prime minister's office before the cabinet meeting was due to start.
